value.rationale: The result identifies a motivated, sharp transition in the validity of continuum second-order approximations for ultra-parallel random-walk coverage of a growing finite cycle. At log(k)~c n^(2/3), a precise non-Gaussian Cramér quartic shift survives; above it the same fluctuation window provably loses tightness while the first-order time remains stable. This is more than the classical Brownian two-Gumbel shape and is a naturally testable distinction between lattice and continuum search models.
